gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's own US store charges the same $699.99 for the SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh, 35.7 lb) as for the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh, 24.9 lb), which works out to $0.35 per Wh against $0.68 per Wh and 56 Wh per lb against 41 Wh per lb.
standout_why: I compared against greenmachineadventures.com (cited), yourpowersetup.com (cited) and outagereadyhq.com's camping guide. Greenmachine already derives Wh per lb for the C1000 Gen 2, DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2 and Elite 100 V2 (about 37 to 45). It has no prices, no cost per Wh and no S2000. Yourpowersetup lists only specs: no price, cost per Wh or recharge hours. Outagereadyhq lists 1 kWh prices (Anker $699.99, DELTA 3 Plus $719, Elite 100 V2 $499) but does not state cost per Wh and does not cover the S2000. No rival works out hours to refill from a kit's own panel. unpluggedwatts.com would not load because of a certificate error, so it is not compared.
decides: For car camping, where 10.8 extra pounds matter less, the S2000 gives about twice the stored energy of the C1000 Gen 2 for the same maker-store price ($0.35/Wh vs $0.68/Wh). That challenges ChatGPT's 'default ~1,000Wh' advice and its prices: it showed the C1000 Gen 2 at $549.99 (B&H) and the S2000 at $749.99 (Best Buy). The trade-off is the S2000's 1,500 W output against the C1000 Gen 2's 2,000 W. If the shopper wants about 1 kWh, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 at $499 is the cheapest per Wh ($0.49). The DELTA 3 Plus is the most expensive per Wh ($0.70) and is currently a pre-order. Its 1,000 W solar input only matters if the shopper carries more than 600 W of panels.
